section: 7. The construction record as bounded corroboration
text:
7. The construction record as bounded corroboration
This reconstruction has access to something most rational reconstructions lack: a contemporaneous record of the programme’s development, in which the belt revisions of Section 6 and the core-attacks of Section 6.2 were logged as they occurred. The record’s evidential role must be bounded carefully, because a development log is a record of authoring, not of scientific discovery, and Lakatos’s own historiography has been criticised precisely for selective narrative reconstruction.
We therefore assign the record a strictly secondary role: the published papers are the primary evidence, and the record corroborates only the temporal order of revisions that the papers independently display. The claim is not that the record “lets the appraisal rest on observed history” — that would invite the selective-narrative charge — but that, where the papers show a conjecture in one state and a theorem in a later state, the record corroborates that the second followed the first under documented adversarial pressure rather than being present from the outset. The contribution of the record is checkability by a third party, not historiographic authority.
The same record makes the programme’s single open seam impossible to overlook, which is itself a mark in the programme’s favour: the deferred demographic test of Section 6.3 is named in the programme’s own papers as the discriminating test it has not run. The frontier is declared, not hidden, and declaring it is part of the appraisal rather than a concession against it.

title: A Progressing Problemshift
section: 8. Scope, limits, and the conflict of interest
text:
8. Scope, limits, and the conflict of interest
The reconstruction’s reach is bounded, and stating the bounds is required by the very discipline it appraises.
First, and most importantly, the appraisal is not a truth-claim about the core. That the programme is theoretically progressing says nothing about whether labour power is the right numéraire or whether Labor-Power Dominance is the right welfare criterion. The framework holds the core immune; the appraisal lives entirely in the belt.
Second, the most dangerous objection is one this paper cannot refute, only scope honestly. Lakatos’s fullest sense of progress requires a corroborated novel fact; by the programme’s own admission its discriminating predictions are as yet uncorroborated. A determined critic may therefore say that the programme is, at most, theoretically progressive and empirically unappraised — a candidate for a progressive problemshift rather than a confirmed one. We accept this. It is the reason the paper’s title claims a progressing problemshift rather than a progressive one, and the reason the deferred demographic test is presented as the registered commitment whose outcome would settle the question. The objection is converted from a refutation into the programme’s stated research frontier; it is not dissolved.
Third, the conflict of interest is real: the author is reconstructing a programme he co-authored. Three mitigations are offered, and their sufficiency is left for the reader to judge. (i) The appraisal rests only on checkable artifacts — the published papers, and secondarily the construction record — so a hostile reader can re-run the reconstruction on the same artifacts and reach a different verdict; the appraisal is exposed to exactly that test, and the author actively invites an independent reconstruction as the proper remedy for residual authorial selection. (ii) The paper reports the programme’s open seam (Sections 6.3, 7) rather than only its successes, and demotes the programme’s most convenient empirical result (Section 6.3). (iii) The appraisal criterion is general and applies symmetrically: an orthodox programme that declared its competitive-efficiency core and exposed its belt to the same scrutiny would pass, and a heterodox programme that concealed its core or rescued it ad hoc would fail. We note, without resting the paper on it, that the orthodox competitive benchmark typically operates as an undeclared default — the asymmetry of Section 3; the point is not that orthodoxy lacks a normative numéraire but that its revealed-preference axiomatics derive a utility representation while leaving the choice of Pareto efficiency as the welfare standard as undeclared as ever. A full development of that comparative claim is deferred.
Fourth, the appraisal is explicitly framework-relative. The verdict “theoretically progressive and non-degenerating” is rendered by Lakatos’s criterion; a different appraisal apparatus could return a different verdict, and we do not hide this. A Laudan problem-solving appraisal, in particular, might be harsher — it would weigh the conceptual problems the programme creates (how to measure reproductive capacity; how to operationalise the dominance criterion) against its problem-solving rate, and a thin early belt could score poorly on that ledger. We choose Lakatos for the scoping reasons of Section 2.4, and concede that the choice is not verdict-neutral; a companion appraisal under a rival framework is legitimate further work, not a threat the present paper must pre-emptively defeat.
Fifth, and most uncomfortably, the paper’s own transparency can be turned against it. A reviewer disposed to refuse heterodox work appraisal a priori — the disposition Section 1 names — can cite the candid concessions here (the pending empirical test, the single content-increasing step, the conflict of interest) as grounds for rejection, and so use the paper’s honesty as the instrument of the very threshold-refusal it protests. We record this without weaponising it: it would be self-sealing, and therefore a violation of this paper’s own discipline, to treat any rejection as confirmation of the thesis. The honest statement is narrower and falsifiable — that this paper’s disclosures are the kind of material an adversarial reading can use to raise the cost of an honest programme relative to a concealed one. That asymmetry of cost is an observation about the sociology of appraisal, offered as such; nothing in the progressivity verdict depends on it.
That deferred claim — that a declared normative core, disciplined by a falsifiable belt and an immanent heuristic, is thereby held to a higher evidential standard than a concealed one — is a natural extension of this reconstruction and a more ambitious thesis than the present one. It is flagged as further work precisely so that it does not inflate the bounded claim made here.

title: A Progressing Problemshift
text:
9. Conclusion
A four-paper heterodox programme admits a Lakatosian reconstruction as one declared hard core, a four-ply falsifiable belt, and one immanent heuristic; and, judged by Lakatos’s own graded criterion, its development to date is theoretically progressive and non-degenerating, with its rival-beating empirical progressivity specified but pending. None of this asserts the truth of the core or the correctness of the policy.
The modesty is the result, not a failure of nerve. It is the largest claim the public artifacts support without auto-goaling the programme’s core — and it is enough to do the one thing heterodox work is usually denied: to place the programme in a form where its merits and demerits can be appraised on the evidence, rather than refused at the threshold. Whether that clears the bar for publication is for the reader to judge; we claim only that it is honest. If there is a portable contribution here beyond the single case, it is a small piece of appraisal vocabulary — the distinction between a progressing problemshift (theoretical content-increase under way, discriminating corroboration registered but pending) and an established progressive one — together with a worked demonstration that the distinction can be drawn against checkable artifacts without either inflating the weaker claim into the stronger or retreating into mere description. A reviewer disposed to refuse heterodox work appraisal will find in these pages the materials to do so; a reviewer willing to appraise it will find a programme that has begun to move, by the mainstream philosophy of science’s own criterion, and has said exactly how far. That a body of heterodox economics can be rendered appraisable in those terms at all — against a checkable record, without overclaiming — is the contribution offered here for the reader’s judgement.
